scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Photographs in the collection originate from Estus Magoon's service in the American Red Scross in Albania in World War I and his work with the International Health Division in various Latin American countries ensuring malaria control and clean water. There are photos of Albania, Costa Rica, and Belize (British Honduras).

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Estus H. Magoon deposited his photographs with the Rockefeller Foundation Archives in 1963.

userestrict.p: The Rockefeller Foundation has title, copyright, and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them. Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish archival material from the collection.

did.unittitle: Estus H. Magoon - World War I and malaria control photographs
did.physdesc: 11 still images: 11 photograph prints. Most photos are mounted. Almost all photos have captions on their backs.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: World War I photographs are of Durazzo, Albania. They show the town, native Albanians, and Serbian soldiers. Other photographs in the file are from Estus Magoon's malaria control and clean water supply work in Latin American countries. There are photos from Costa Rica and Belize (British Honduras). - Catpions paraphrased from photos and added description: 4. Durazzo, Albania, 1916. Serbians and Romanian Romani person near an old wall; 5. Durazzo, Albania, 1916. Native Albanians. Serbians are seated; 6. Durazzo, Albania, 1916. Street scene in the business district; 7. Durazzo, Albania, 1915. Serbian soldiers in retreat; 11. Costa Rica, 1929. Construction of reinforced slab of concrete for sanitary privy. Mold was made in Costa Rica and sent to other Central American countries. Metal molds were made in Venezuela for the same purpose; 12. Tres Rios, Costa Rica. Completed sanitary privy; 13. San Lucas, penal colony island of Costa Rica. Anopheles control measures. Background: shallow water tank used for curing cement sand tiles. Foreground: machine used to form the tiles before they are placed on the shelves; 14. San Antonio, British Honduras. Indigenous home; 15. Belize, British Honduras. Mahogany logs being towed up Haulover Creek to sawmill at Belize; 16. Nearly identical image of #15.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Some of the captions on the photographs use terms to describe people of Romani and Indigenous heritage that may be considered offensive or outdated.

did.physdesc: 3 still images: 3 photograph prints. Photos are mounted and have captions.
